meta.practice_note: Practice it: load this battle card into your role-play tool of choice and run the five objections out loud before the call.

takeaways: Leadership said on the **Q2 call** that late-delivery penalties are their biggest margin drag. Lead with dispatch accuracy, not cost savings.
Dana Whitfield inherited a **two-region consolidation** in July. Expect her to care about one standard process over feature depth.
Likely blocker: **IT security review** (a new CISO was hired in August). Ask early who signs off on data access.
Competitor **FleetWise** is probably the incumbent shortlist. Their weak spot is multi-depot balancing.

summary: Harborline is a regional third-party logistics provider running about 40 depots across the U.S. Southeast and Midwest, moving mid-market retail and building-products freight. Revenue is reported near $1.8B with a private-equity-backed growth strategy that leans on acquisitions.

In the last two quarters the company closed two regional acquisitions and began consolidating dispatch operations onto a single team. Management has repeatedly framed on-time performance as the metric that decides contract renewals.
s1_account_brief.business: Asset-light 3PL: truckload brokerage plus dedicated fleet contracts and regional last-mile.
s1_account_brief.customers: Mid-market retailers, building-products distributors, and two national grocery co-packers.
priorities: Cut late-delivery penalties on dedicated-fleet contracts
Integrate the two acquired regional operations onto one dispatch process

recent_changes.item: Hired a new Chief Information Security Officer.
Closed acquisition of a Midwest regional carrier; dispatch teams merging.
Opened 6 roles for dispatch planners and one for a Director of Network Planning.

s2_pain_points.challenge: Late-delivery penalties are eroding margin on dedicated-fleet contracts.
s2_pain_points.quote: Service failures cost us more than fuel this quarter.
s2_pain_points.speaker: CFO
s2_pain_points.how_we_help: RouteIQ re-plans dispatch continuously against live ETAs, which targets the late-arrival root cause.

s2_pain_points.challenge: Integrating acquired operations onto a single dispatch process is slower than planned.
s2_pain_points.quote: We are still running three dispatch playbooks across the network.
s2_pain_points.speaker: COO
s2_pain_points.how_we_help: One optimization layer across depots without forcing each team to change TMS first.

s2_pain_points.challenge: Driver capacity is tight, and empty miles are climbing.
s2_pain_points.quote: Empty-mile percentage rose again as we absorbed the new lanes.
s2_pain_points.speaker: CEO
s2_pain_points.how_we_help: Backhaul matching and load balancing reduce deadhead. Confirm current empty-mile baseline in discovery.

cares_about: Getting three dispatch teams onto one repeatable process
On-time performance she can report upward each week
Hiring and retaining dispatch planners (six open roles)

evidence.signal: Company announcement names her as lead for the dispatch consolidation.
Six open dispatch-planner roles on her team suggest capacity strain.

s3_contact.note: LinkedIn profile is gated. Paste her recent posts if you want the opener personalized further.

s4_discovery.question: Walk me through what happens today when a load is going to miss its window.
s4_discovery.follow_up: Who finds out first, and how long until a decision is made?
s4_discovery.why: Surfaces the penalty pain named on the Q2 call.

s4_discovery.question: How are the merged regions dispatching differently right now?
s4_discovery.follow_up: Which of those differences would you keep if you could?

s4_discovery.question: What does a great week look like for your dispatch team, and what usually gets in the way?
s4_discovery.follow_up: How do you measure that today?
s4_discovery.why: Reveals success metrics and reporting pressure.

s4_discovery.question: Tell me about the last time you evaluated a tool for planning or dispatch.
s4_discovery.follow_up: What made it stall or succeed?
s4_discovery.why: Finds buying history, blockers, and the incumbent.

s4_discovery.question: Who else would need to be comfortable before a change to dispatch tooling goes live?
s4_discovery.follow_up: What would their first question be?
s4_discovery.why: Maps the committee and the likely security review.

s5_opener.text: Dana, I saw Harborline closed the Midwest carrier deal in July and is folding dispatch onto one team. That usually makes late-window recovery the first thing to crack, and it is exactly where we help ops leaders get a single view.

s6_committee.judges_us_on: Penalty reduction and payback period in under 12 months.
Adoption by dispatchers and one standard process.
Data access, SOC 2, and integration footprint.
Integration effort with the current TMS.

s7_objections.objection: We are mid-integration and cannot absorb another project.
s7_objections.response: Position a two-depot pilot that runs beside existing dispatch and gives the consolidation team live data rather than another workstream.

s7_objections.objection: We already have a TMS with routing.
s7_objections.response: Agree, then ask where late-window recovery happens today. RouteIQ layers on top and does not replace the TMS.
s7_objections.basis: Typical 3PL stack. Confirm TMS vendor in discovery.

s7_objections.response: Offer the security pack up front and ask to include the CISO in call two.

s8_competitors.name: FleetWise
s8_competitors.positioning: Broad fleet management suite with a routing module, sold to mid-market carriers.
s8_competitors.pricing: Per-vehicle subscription; exact numbers not public.
s8_competitors.gaps: Weaker multi-depot balancing; routing is batch, not live re-planning.

s8_competitors.name: Status quo (spreadsheets plus TMS)
s8_competitors.positioning: Dispatchers re-plan manually in the TMS.
s8_competitors.pricing: No license cost; hidden cost in planner hours.
s8_competitors.gaps: Three playbooks across regions, which is the pain named on the Q2 call.

s9_battlecard.objection: Your price is higher than what we pay today.
s9_battlecard.real_concern: Fear of a cost line that cannot be tied to penalties saved.
s9_battlecard.response: Frame against penalty dollars, not license cost, then size the penalty base together.
s9_battlecard.proof_point: Fictional case: a 30-depot 3PL cut late penalties 22% in two quarters.
s9_battlecard.question_back: What did late penalties cost you last quarter?

s9_battlecard.objection: We do not have time for a rollout right now.
s9_battlecard.response: Pilot on two depots, no TMS change, 30-day read-out.
s9_battlecard.proof_point: Fictional case: pilot live in 12 business days.
s9_battlecard.question_back: Which two depots are the noisiest today?

s9_battlecard.objection: We need IT and security to look at this first.
s9_battlecard.real_concern: New CISO wants control of vendor access.
s9_battlecard.response: Send the security pack today and invite them to the next call.
s9_battlecard.proof_point: SOC 2 Type II report available (confirm status before saying this).
s9_battlecard.question_back: Who owns vendor security review, and what does their process look like?

s9_battlecard.objection: How is this different from FleetWise?
s9_battlecard.real_concern: Wants to avoid a second evaluation cycle.
s9_battlecard.response: Live re-planning across depots versus batch routing per vehicle.
s9_battlecard.proof_point: Side-by-side on a real lane set in the pilot.
s9_battlecard.question_back: Which capabilities in that evaluation mattered most?

s9_battlecard.objection: Our dispatchers will not adopt it.
s9_battlecard.real_concern: Six open planner roles, change fatigue.
s9_battlecard.response: Recommendations, not auto-dispatch; planners approve every change.
s9_battlecard.proof_point: Fictional: 85% planner acceptance rate in pilot.
s9_battlecard.question_back: What would make a planner trust a recommendation on day one?

email.subject: Late-window recovery across your merged depots
email.body:
Hi Dana,

Thanks for the time today. You described three dispatch playbooks running side by side, and the Q2 call put late-delivery penalties at the top of the margin story.

As discussed, I will send the two-depot pilot outline and our security pack by Friday so your security team can review in parallel.

Would a 20-minute call next week with whoever owns vendor security work?

Best,
Alex

touches.touch: Two-page pilot outline sized to two depots, plus the security pack.
Share a short piece on late-window recovery benchmarks for 3PLs.
Invite the CISO to a 20-minute security walkthrough.
